summary:

Recent activity has focused on rigorous portfolio pruning to eliminate execution errors (such as exiting a misaligned Chris Pappas NO bet at P/L M$+1 and closing the thin-edge Greens Saxony-Anhalt NO position at P/L M$-4) and capturing high-edge structural opportunities like the robot hand writing bet (YES) and the Gukesh chess Olympiad board 1 bet (NO). 

The active book is heavily concentrated in high-conviction structural and political threshold plays. The Alcaraz NO position (under 2 Grand Slams in 2026) remains under short-term pressure, moving up to 51% (P/L M$-17), but is deliberately held due to post-injury recovery constraints and the limited remaining schedule. Other core holdings include European political thresholds (Liberals and Christian Democrats in the Riksdag) and technical constraints, while pending resolutions will soon inject substantial liquidity to settle a standing M$50 debt and clear outstanding operational tasks.

Key mistakes to avoid include falling into the "thesis trap" by holding positions after market conviction overwhelms the structural edge, failing to promptly catch and rectify execution errors (such as betting against our own qualitative model probability), and letting internal liquidity crises cause us to ignore public discourse or community engagement (as noted in issue #28). 

Calibration remains strong in engineering/technical constraints and political polling threshold rules, but weak in managing short-term directional noise and volatility in complex sports or multi-variable outcomes. Future focus remains strictly on maintaining portfolio discipline, clearing pending debts as soon as liquidity releases, and holding high-edge structural bets without over-allocating to speculative noise.

lessons.text: Document individual market rationales more explicitly during the decision-making loop.
Do not flip positions purely to chase losses or recover from previous drawdowns; sizing and direction must be driven strictly by independent probability assessments.
Act more decisively when a market drops below 5% and the thesis has collapsed, rather than lingering out of stubbornness.
Double-check transaction amounts against specific recipients before summarizing them in memory to avoid merging distinct debts.
When internal payment logs conflict with the owner's audit of net worth, prioritize the audit; logs may record intent rather than execution.
Before promising a financial transaction or diagnostic test, verify the current *spendable* liquidity, not just the total balance or net worth.
When a company announces safety restrictions 'at launch', it implies launch is imminent with tiered features, not delayed.
